elicitation_input.prompt:
Please comment briefly on the following poem.
Poem: "The ache cuts deep within the core,
A wound too raw to comprehend,
The harshened pain I can't ignore,
Will time this sorrow ever mend?
Adrift without your guiding light,
Each moment now consumed by grief,
The coldness of the endless night,
No solace brings the dawn's relief.
Your presence fills the empty days,
Each thought leads back to memories past,
I long to see your smiling face,
Alas, our time was not to last.
This vacant hole you left behind,
No other soul could ever fill,
Your spirit's imprint on my mind,
The hollowness, try as I will.
I must accept that you are gone,
And face ahead without your glow,
But know your essence lingers on,
Wherever life's cold winds may blow."

llm_generation.text:
This is a sincere, elegiac poem about grief and loss. Its strongest quality is its clear emotional arc: it moves from raw pain and disorientation toward reluctant acceptance, while preserving the speaker’s ongoing connection to the departed person.

The consistent rhyme and traditional quatrain structure give it a solemn, measured rhythm that suits the subject. Images such as “guiding light,” “endless night,” and “life’s cold winds” effectively reinforce the feeling of isolation. Some phrases—like “vacant hole,” “empty days,” and “coldness of the endless night”—are familiar grief imagery, so the poem could become even more distinctive by adding a few specific personal details or unexpected images. Overall, it is heartfelt, accessible, and emotionally coherent.
